run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The storefront entry point is broken by a faulty change to the frontend-proxy Deployment. At 2026-11-23T22:37:44Z, one minute after the whole demo was started, the frontend-proxy Deployment was updated by the API-server-recorded manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' (revision 1 -> 2) and a new ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 replaced frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5; the only pod-template difference is an extra environment variable FRONTEND_HOST=localhost appended after the correct FRONTEND_HOST=frontend (image and 65Mi memory limit unchanged). Requests through the new frontend-proxy pod immediately start failing: spans of service frontend-proxy with error=true / http.status_code=0 lasting ~15s, nested GET -> 'router frontend egress' -> GET chains that re-enter the proxy itself, and load-generator GET returning HTTP 504 with otel.status_code=ERROR starting 2026-11-23T22:37:45.539Z, whereas the same frontend routes returned HTTP 200 up to 2026-11-23T22:37:45.3Z. At query time (22:39:20Z, after the authorized window's 22:37:56Z end) the new pod is not Ready, the frontend-proxy Service has only notReadyAddresses, and the container reports restartCount 3 with current and previous termination reason OOMKilled (exit 137) - i.e. the self-directed proxy loop exhausts its 65Mi limit and crash-loops. All 26 other application pods were Ready with 0 restarts and no OOM marks, and flagd flags are all 'off', so the fault is confined to the frontend-proxy Deployment's pod template.

claims.text: At 2026-11-23T22:37:44Z the Deployment frontend-proxy (namespace astronomy-shop) was updated to revision 2 by the manager recorded as 'OpenAPI-Generator' (previous/other writer was 'helm' at 22:36:55Z); a new ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 was created at 22:37:44Z while frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 was scaled 1->0 at 22:37:45Z and its pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-7284r was deleted.

The only pod-template difference between frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 and frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 is the container env: the new ReplicaSet (and therefore Deployment frontend-proxy revision 2) holds a second FRONTEND_HOST entry with value 'localhost' after the original FRONTEND_HOST=frontend; the image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy) and the resources.limits.memory 65Mi are identical in both ReplicaSets.

Baseline before the rollout: frontend-proxy spans in traces from 22:37:40Z to 22:37:45.3Z carry http.status_code=200 (e.g. 'router frontend egress' 27,681us and 10,699us), and the frontend service served GET /api/recommendations and GET /api/data with http.status_code=200 and gRPC status 0.

From 2026-11-23T22:37:45.539Z, spans of service frontend-proxy record error=true with http.status_code=0 and ~15.0s duration (14,998,296-14,999,313us) on operation 'GET' and 'router frontend egress', nested inside each other (GET -> router frontend egress -> GET -> router frontend egress), i.e. the proxy's frontend route re-enters the proxy itself instead of reaching the frontend Service.

The same failing trace shows the client side: load-generator span operation 'GET' with status tags error=true, http.status_code=504 and otel.status_code=ERROR after 15,005,521us (trace be2d7102b0c3a83700375488541f0b84), started 22:37:45.539Z.

No frontend service span appears in the sampled traces after the failing request begins (only the trace starting 22:37:45.331Z, before the old pod's SIGTERM at 22:37:45.386Z, contains frontend spans), and the failing trace be2d7102b0c3a83700375488541f0b84 contains only frontend-proxy and load-generator spans.

The new frontend-proxy pod logged that envoy finished loading 9 clusters and started workers at 2026-11-23T22:37:44.843-844Z, and the old pod logged ENVOY_SIGTERM and 'exiting' at 22:37:45.386-399Z, so the failures begin after the new pod took over the only proxy endpoint.

At query time (observed 2026-11-23T22:39:20Z, after the authorized window end 22:37:56Z) pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-k5rhx has Ready=False and ContainersReady=False (reason ContainersNotReady, lastTransitionTime 22:39:15Z), restartCount 3, current container terminated with exitCode 137 reason OOMKilled at finishedAt 22:39:14Z and lastState terminated reason OOMKilled exitCode 137 at finishedAt 22:38:31Z.

At query time the Service/Endpoints frontend-proxy holds pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-k5rhx (10.244.234.188) only under notReadyAddresses, so the frontend-proxy Service has no ready backend; Service frontend still has ready address 10.244.7.215 (pod frontend-6859c775df-8rz6v).

All other 26 pods in namespace astronomy-shop were Ready with restartCount 0 and no terminated/OOM container state in the same query, including frontend-6859c775df-8rz6v, cart, checkout, payment, product-catalog, ad, recommendation and load-generator; at 22:37:50Z kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total was 0 for every pod in the namespace, including the then-serving frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-7284r.

The flagd-config ConfigMap holds only flags whose defaultVariant is 'off'/0 (paymentFailure, cartFailure, adFailure, productCatalogFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, emailMemoryLeak, llmRateLimitError, etc.), so no feature flag was switched on at the time of the check.

The self-referential route caused by FRONTEND_HOST=localhost in Deployment frontend-proxy makes envoy proxy the storefront route to its own listener; the resulting recursive requests pile up memory in the 65Mi container until it is OOMKilled (exit 137) and crash-loops, leaving the frontend-proxy Service with no ready endpoint and clients receiving 504/timeouts. This is the mechanism linking the observed pod-template change to the observed errors and OOM kills.

A feature-flag fault injection (flagd) was considered and rejected as the cause of the frontend-proxy failure: every flag in flagd-config has defaultVariant 'off'/0 and no frontend-proxy-related flag exists.
A NetworkPolicy blocking traffic between services was considered and rejected: reading kind networkpolicies for namespace astronomy-shop returned no objects.

A lowered memory limit was considered and rejected as the trigger of the OOMKilled container: both frontend-proxy ReplicaSets declare resources.limits.memory 65Mi, so the limit did not change with revision 2; only the env differs.

Application pods other than frontend-proxy showed no failure of their own: the sampled spans around the change show frontend, ad, cart, recommendation and product-catalog operations with http.status_code=200 / rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and their pods were Ready with 0 restarts; they were checked and found healthy for this cause.

Remove the injected duplicate FRONTEND_HOST=localhost env entry from Deployment frontend-proxy so its pod template matches revision 1 (FRONTEND_HOST=frontend) and roll the Deployment; the new pod should then pass readiness and the Service should regain a ready endpoint.

gaps: The authorized window ends 2026-11-23T22:37:56Z, only ~11s after the faulty Deployment update (22:37:44Z); behaviour after that time is known only from object state read at query time (pod status at 22:39:20Z showing OOMKilled at 22:38:31Z and 22:39:14Z), not from in-window telemetry.

The rendered envoy configuration (envoy.tmpl.yaml baked into image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy, no ConfigMap mount in the pod spec) could not be read, so the exact substitution result of the duplicate FRONTEND_HOST entries is inferred from the nested frontend-proxy spans rather than read directly.

Prometheus series traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned no samples inside the window (get_series empty, increase() no_data), so no error-rate or latency time series could be computed; per-service error assessment relies on Jaeger samples and pod state.
load-generator application logs could not be read (fetch_pod_logs returned SOURCE_FORBIDDEN for load-generator-69fcd4cb96-d6z2f); its failure is evidenced only by the 504 span.
The change_history integration is not configured in this Run, so who or what applied the frontend-proxy update beyond the API server's recorded manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 22:37:44Z is unknown.

No container memory series existed for the new pod inside the window (only frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-7284r at ~18.7MiB at 22:37:56Z), so the memory growth preceding the OOM kills was not observed directly.
next_steps: Confirm the fix by watching FrontendProxy pod readiness, the frontend-proxy Service endpoints and load-generator HTTP status codes after removing the duplicate FRONTEND_HOST env entry.
If available later, read frontend-proxy container logs and the envoy admin stats (upstream 5xx, rq_timeout) for the period after 22:37:56Z to confirm the self-loop and memory growth.
Verify with the team that owns the 'OpenAPI-Generator' manager identity why it patched the frontend-proxy Deployment pod template.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
